thread:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — Acme ticket #4567. They see 2-3x token counts on some requests and intermittent 300-600ms latency spikes. App is in eu-west, but we see calls landing in us-east. Started ~2026-02-23 11:23 PST.

Samir Patel: Copy. Can you paste any raw headers or a sample span?

Acme Admin: Here are the request IDs we captured from our side: client_req=cr-9a1b, server_calls: srv-eu-111 and srv-us-222 for the same client request. We sent only to our eu endpoint (no client-side region override).

Support Bot: ingest-log: cr-9a1b -> routed to eu-west-1 at t=0ms; hedged attempt fired at t=55ms -> routed to us-east-1. Responses: eu responded at 180ms, us at 210ms. Both produced token usage events.

Will Gomez: That smells like hedged retries + aggressive timeout. Any SDK config attached?

Acme Admin: SDK config attached from their code: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  region: 'eu-west-1',
  hedgedRetries: true,
  hedgedTimeoutMs: 50,
  maxAttempts: 3,
  backoffJitter: 0
});
```
They set hedgedTimeoutMs=50 and jitter disabled.

Samir Patel: OK. Root cause looks like: hedgedRetries triggers parallel/fallback attempts when primary doesn't accept within 50ms. With jitter=0 and small timeout, the hedged attempt races to another region (smart-routing currently considers cross-region fallback if local capacity/p95 not met). The result: two downstream model invocations for the same client request -> double tokenization/compute billing and duplicated latency events.

Maria Chen: Customer impact: higher cost and confusing billing, plus visible latency spikes. They want immediate mitigation and a repro so they can validate.

Will Gomez: Quick mitigations we can propose: 
- Ask them to set hedgedRetries=false OR increase hedgedTimeoutMs to >=200ms and enable jitter (backoffJitter > 0).
- Use client option preferLocalRegion: true (pins route to eu unless explicit failover).
- As a platform short-term: add server-side dedupe for duplicate hedged invocations within a 300ms window for the same client_req id (needs infra ticket).

Samir Patel: Repro steps for support to validate locally: 
1) Run stress loop from eu host with the SDK config above.
2) Observe routing in logs: look for X-Redwood-Route and X-Request-Id pairs.
3) Confirm two downstream calls for one client_req.

Command snippet we gave Acme: 
```bash
# simulate hedged behavior quickly
node -e "const c=require('./client'); for(i=0;i<10;i++) c.call({prompt:'hello', region:'eu-west-1'})"
# watch platform logs: grep cr-9a1b
```

Support Bot: Note: billing currently counts each model invocation separately. No dedupe in usage pipeline. Raising billing dispute will require support+finance review.

Maria Chen: Action items: 
- Support: send quick config patch to customer (disable hedged OR increase timeout + enable jitter) and request they retest. (Assigned: Support Bot)
- SDK: add safer defaults in next minor: hedgedTimeoutMs default -> 200ms, backoffJitter default -> 0.2, and add docs warning about cross-region fallbacks. (Assigned: SDK Bot)
- Infra/Product: evaluate server-side dedupe windows and billing dedupe feasibility. (Assigned: Will/Platform)

SDK Bot: Note for SDK PR: example default change diff: 
```diff
- hedgedTimeoutMs: 50,
- backoffJitter: 0,
+ hedgedTimeoutMs: 200,
+ backoffJitter: 0.2,
```
We'll also add a note to docs: "Hedged retries can cause multiple model invocations and duplicate usage charges if cross-region fallback is enabled."

Acme Admin: Thanks — we've applied hedgedRetries=false for now. We'll confirm if billing blips stop and share logs. Appreciate the fast triage. :pray:

Will Gomez: I'll open PLAT-983 (dedupe + billing review) and attach traces. Samir — can you add a short retro note on whether routing should consider client pin headers before firing hedged attempts?

Samir Patel: Yep will do. Also adding a unit-test in SDK to ensure hedged=on + preferLocal true pins attempts to same region unless a hard failure occurs.

Maria Chen: Thanks team. Keep thread updated with customer confirmation. :thumbsup:
